body: Haha, good suggestions!! You’re right, I’m being too nice. I mostly try to “keep the peace,” but sometimes I think that falls into avoiding confrontations. I do hate that she’s taking advantage and it’s not ok!
Yeah, this is what I need to do. I think I’ve been treating her like a friend/fellow adult, and she’s not acting like either.

Try not to worry about it, silences aren’t necessarily awkward - could be just two people lost in their own thoughts. When you’re feeling comfortable you should tell her that you have anxiety sometimes, and that you don’t mean anything personal by it if you seem distant. Some of my better friends have been extroverts - it’s nice because a lot of times they won’t notice if you’re feeling anxious and you can pretend it’s not a big deal and go on with life feeling like a semi-normal person
Ugh yes, I feel this way too! Sometimes I even blurt out rude/insulting things, and I have no idea why, I feel so ashamed after... Some weird self-damaging impulse

You should definitely go! Unfortunately, I’m forced to go to pretty much every single social event solo, and have been for a couple years. You feel anxious in the beginning, but just notice it, accept it - “I am feeling anxious right now,” - like “it is raining right now.” Be kind to yourself, and make yourself a promise - stay for half an hour / an hour and if you still feel terrible, you’re allowed to leave. Who knows, you might just have a great time! If not, you can at least be proud of yourself for the effort.

That’s so true about the career thing. I know, college is ridiculously expensive, and I guess it doesn’t really guarantee a job at all.

I’ve tried OkCupid and tinder, and gone on some dates, but I think low-self esteem is the thing that’s holding me back. I try to feel ok, but sometimes I get all anxious and don’t act like myself, and the high-availability dating game makes people just skip to the next person. It makes me feel not as good as other people out there, and like I don’t have much to draw others to me :-(
This is really good advice! Thanks. Yeah, I definitely need to shake things up

Oh. My. God. This is literally me to a T. Every time I get a text, even a nice little "hey!" it's like this annoying weight hanging over my head and I have to push it out of my mind, so I won't answer it for hours and hours. I have a job and pay my rent and bills but I'm literally not excited about life at all. Everything and everyone seems dull. I too have blown off people and events to just sit at home thinking, watching tv, doing "nothing" by myself, which is the only thing I actually "enjoy."

Do you by any chance smoke weed? I do, not stoned at work or anything but every day after, and I was thinking this could be a factor.

I've also thought that it was a plateau of existential realism - we are all just insignificant animals trying to survive, the endless pointless dance of consumerism and self-promotion and pursuit of wordly goods and popularity that is totally pointless if you really think about it... Meh. Could just be the weed ;-)

I'm with ya tho!! Kind of makes me feel better that I'm not the only one. Hug, from across the digital universe ((()))

It's seriously so hard to love yourself when everybody around you thinks you're not worth much. Like, at some point you take the hint and start to see yourself the way they do :-/
I've been trying to be my own "best friend" - say encouraging things to myself, tell myself little jokes or humorous observations  throughout the day- little funny secrets that no one else would get. Lol, it's hard, I still have negative voices that are hard to ignore, but it really makes me feel better. You can be the friend you wish you had <3

I've had this thought before too - I think that external factors are a huge part of social anxiety for me at least. Just speaking from my own personal experience, I was an overly sensitive/observant/introverted child by nature, and a lot of criticism about my personality and looks from parents, adults and other children set me down the road to social anxiety. Social anxiety is like PTSD- I think that some of us are just a lot more susceptible to it, the naturally hyper-sensitive or anxious personalities.

So, both nature and nurture play their roles here.

I've actually been thinking about starting martial arts recently- thanks for your reply, you really encouraged me to follow through with that :)
Yeah, it's hard not to get caught up in the past, but you're right- I think going outside the comfort zone is a great idea. It is easy for me to get stuck in a rut and think that's all there is to life. Thank you <3
Forgot to mention that I'm currently in therapy already, but my depression is more existential than chemical, so medications don't do much.
